story.what_it_does: Infosys is a large Indian IT services company that serves clients worldwide. It earned ₹1,78,650 crore of revenue in FY2026 with about 3.28 lakh employees. Its revenue comes from client contracts, many of them fixed-price, and it now reports a growing share from AI services.
story.plans: Management guides FY27 operating margin of 20% to 22% and has cut its FY27 revenue growth guidance from 1.5%-3.5% to 1%-2% in constant currency. It plans to hire 20,000 freshers, build a 6,000-strong Frontier Engineer team over the next few years, and expects a net-new mega deal to add about 1% growth in FY28. It also aims to become climate positive by 2030.
story.moat: The notes show scale, with large deal wins of $14.9 bn in FY26 and a ₹1,30,017 crore backlog of remaining performance obligations. Margins of around 21% and steady free cash flow of $900 mn+ per quarter suggest a solid position. But clients are pushing for lower prices because of AI productivity, which the notes show is eroding pricing power.

scenarios.story: AI services keep scaling from 8.2% to 10.5% of revenue and the net-new mega deal lifts FY28 growth. Large deal wins stay strong while margins hold near 21%.
signals_to_watch: AI revenue share of total revenue after the 10.5% in Q2 FY27
Large deal TCV versus the $5.2 bn in Q2 FY27

scenarios.story: Growth stays low at about 1% to 2% in constant currency while margins stay within the 20% to 22% range. Pricing pressure and weakness in Retail and Hi-Tech offset deal wins and AI gains.
signals_to_watch: Constant-currency revenue growth versus the 1% to 2% guidance

scenarios.story: Pricing deflation at renewals deepens and client reductions spread beyond the European manufacturer, forcing more guidance cuts. Wage costs and AI investment then squeeze margins toward the low end of the range.
